hand.title: Daily Hand

events.text: You raised before the cards were dealt. Your opponent called.
Flop — 7, 5, 5. You bet. Your opponent raised you back.
Turn — Queen. Your opponent bet out. You called.

wrongReasons: J 5 plays similarly, but the correct hand pairs a specific board card that J 5 doesn't. Look at which hole card ranks actually appear on the board.
With only two pair, 7 3 wouldn't commit chips across multiple streets. This betting line requires a genuinely made hand from the flop onward.
With only one pair, 4 8 wouldn't commit chips across multiple streets. This betting line requires a genuinely made hand from the flop onward.
hand.explanation:
Answer: 5 A

Your opponent flopped three of a kind and raised the flop immediately to build the pot. Sets are too strong to slow-play — they pushed their advantage on every street.
